output.brief: VA-220 failures are coming from Pellacott's 2026-built valves, not from the new installers or firmware 4.2. Brenmoor's lab found 11% of unused 2026 Pellacott valves leaking at the seat, against 1% of 2025 Pellacott valves and 0% of Durrant-Hale valves. Claim rates were about the same across installer and firmware groups. The leak-test rig was out of service from January 2026, and no VA-220 test program was loaded on any other rig. The 2026 certificates repeat four fixed sequences of values, some already used in November 2025. So the certificates do not reflect real tests. Pellacott's score rose because the score rewards complete, clean certificates, not real testing. I am quite sure of this. Still open: whether the seal change or the Line 3 move caused the defect (they can't be separated), and whether other suppliers' records are also unreliable. Next steps: do not release the six held lots on new certificates. Quarantine 2026 Pellacott stock and suspend dock-to-stock. Release stock only after Brenmoor's own helium testing. Drop the installer remediation plan and chargebacks. Secure alternative supply from Durrant-Hale to avoid the line stoppage. Audit other suppliers' records and require rig logs for score credit. Investigate the seal and line change.
